verdict:
KILL - and the kill is the doctrinally clean one: we agree with the street. Not 'the street exists', not 'seventeen analysts', not 'twenty-three percent short'. The street's own number for the period this thesis turns on already contains the deceleration the thesis called decisive.

THE DIVERGENCE TEST, WHICH IS THE VERDICT. Full-year 2026 consolidated revenue guidance, from the Q2 release I fetched directly, is $450-500 million. The street's FY26 revenue consensus sits at roughly $459M - the bottom of the company's own guide - and FY26 EPS consensus has been cut from $2.90 to $2.59. The thesis named 'is H2 below H1?' as the question. The street already answers yes. There is no divergence to trade, and a verdict that cannot state the street's number beside ours has not done the work - here it can, and they are the same number. That is the finding.

THE COVERAGE VIOLATION I AM CORRECTING. Our red bench wrote finding 6 as '17 covering analysts, consensus target $223-279, and 21.6-23.3% short interest - CONFIRMED, FATAL to court-worthiness', and then leaned on it in the strongest-kill paragraph. That is a flat DIVERGENCE-NOT-COVERAGE violation: coverage says this name is MEASURED, not that it is measured correctly, and a 23% short interest against $1.87B of cash and a deep-in-the-money convert is a squeeze mechanic, which the taxonomy maps to TIMING and SIZE, never to a rejection. Blue caught it and overturned it, correctly, and then did the work red should have done by going and getting the street's number. The verdict is re-based onto that number. Note the asymmetry that makes this the better outcome: because this name is heavily covered, our agreement with the street is GRADEABLE against an external anchor - in an orphan the same conclusion would have been scored against our own fair value and would have been an artifact.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING IN THE BUSINESS, FROM THE FILING. Q2 LEU segment revenue $153.4M against $125.7M, but that is uranium: SWU revenue fell $25.7M to $100.0M on a 23% volume decline, offset by a first-ever $53.4M of uranium sales. Cost of sales rose 36% to $101.8M. Gross margin in the segment went 40.3% to 33.6%. And the sentence neither bench cited is the one that carries the mechanism: SWU volumes fell 23% while 'the average price of SWU sold' rose only 3% and 'the average unit cost of SWU sold' rose 13% - and over six months, price +16% against unit cost +23%. Realised price is rising and unit cost is rising faster. That is a genuine margin squeeze with a documented cause: the TENEX transitional supply contract carries 2018 pricing but Russian Decree No. 1516 extended the rescission of TENEX's US export licence through 31 December 2027, so replacement SWU comes from Orano at a market formula. Technical Solutions ran a $1.7M gross LOSS in the quarter (against +$3.2M), though six-month TS gross profit is still positive at $1.9M on revenue up 8.3% - so red's 'fixed price plus negative margin' framing is a quarterly base effect at the six-month level, exactly as blue said.

THE MOAT-REFUTATION CHECK (2026-08-18 rule), WHICH CUTS FOR THE COMPANY. The bear instinct on enrichment is 'new Western capacity is coming, the scarcity premium dies'. Check the price series before crediting that: realised SWU prices are UP 3% in the quarter and 16% over six months, and the volume decline is supply-blocked by a Russian export decree, not demand-destroyed. Capacity expansion into a market that is absorbing it at rising prices is a growing market, not a bear case. The bear case here is narrower and more specific - unit cost is outrunning realised price - and it is the one datum the desk should track.

WHERE ELSE OUR BENCHES ERRED. Red's headline FVRR/masking kill was an artifact (the reconciliation is disclosed in both venues and now ties exactly), and its own KG candidate would have a near-1.0 false-positive rate on every ASC 606 filer with IDIQ or contingent volumes. Red leaned on a USAspending null it had itself graded FIRED-WEAK. Red's customs read (zero UF6/EUP consignee arrivals) cannot distinguish supply blockage from connector failure with an empty consignee list. Blue, in turn, corrected red's cost numbers with an intersegment-contaminated base - the second consecutive batch in which the auditing bench itself needed auditing. What both benches got right and I sustain in full: the cap structure. 19,233,658 Class A plus 719,200 Class B = 19,952,858 shares; convert principals are $402.5M and $805.0M (not the thesis's $350M/$700M, which were pre-greenshoe), 4.128M plus 3.506M = 7.63M shares of if-converted dilution (+38.3%), no capped call or note hedge anywhere in the 10-Q, and an if-converted EV of ~$3.43B = ~17.2x annualised gross profit.

BETA-CARRIER DISCIPLINE ON THE GATE. The ledger carries alert_below $100 on a '10x recurring gross profit' basis. LEU's tape is dominated by the nuclear/enrichment complex - red's own read was that roughly two-thirds of the drawdown is complex beta, with NLR down 35%. A price gate on that tape is self-triggering: $100 prints when the whole complex sells off, which is not when this specific business got cheaper relative to its own economics. It must be re-specified as review-only with a relative condition, and the real reopen must be event- and print-shaped.
blue_ruling:
PARTIALLY OVERTURNED - blue overturned three of red's seven findings, including the strongest-single-kill paragraph, and replaced them with the only kill in this record that survives audit (we agree with the street). I re-fetched the primaries per BLUE-CORRECTIONS-AUDITED and the audit splits.

PASSES: blue's backlog overturn. The 10-Q states verbatim that the company 'does not include unexercised options or potential services under indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity agreements in its remaining performance obligations', total RPO is 'approximately $0.8 billion and $0.6 billion' at 6/30/26 and 12/31/25 'and extend to 2030', with the LEU segment alone at approximately $0.7 billion, and the word backlog appears exactly once (as a fresh-start intangible). The Q2 press release, which I fetched directly, states total backlog of $4.5 billion extending to 2040, discloses that the LEU backlog includes 'approximately $3.0 billion in contingent LEU and HALEU sales commitments, a $2.4 billion of which are under definitive agreements', and separately reports Technical Solutions backlog of approximately $0.8 billion including unfunded amounts and unexercised options. So the reconciliation ties, and more cleanly than blue managed it: $4.5B total less ~$0.8B TS (unfunded/options, excluded by the quoted rule) less ~$3.0B contingent = ~$0.7B firm, which is exactly the LEU-segment RPO in the 10-Q. Nothing was concealed; red's multi_venue FIRE mis-fires and its FVRR framing dies. (Blue's own arithmetic was sloppy - it treated the 10-Q's $0.8B total RPO as if it were the TS IDIQ - but it reached the right place.)

FAILS: blue's correction of red's cost finding. Blue wrote that the LEU segment ran revenue $131.8M -> $153.4M (+16.4%), cost of sales $79.3M -> $101.8M (+28.4%), gross profit $52.5M -> $51.6M, and used that to call red's numbers a mix artifact. Those 2025 figures are the segment-note TOTALS INCLUDING intersegment revenue ($6.1M), intersegment cost of sales ($4.3M) and intersegment gross profit ($1.8M), compared against 2026 figures that carry none. The MD&A like-for-like table reads LEU revenue $125.7M -> $153.4M (+22%), cost of sales $75.0M -> $101.8M (+36%), gross profit $50.7M -> $51.6M (+2%). Red's $75.0M base and its +36% were verbatim correct; blue manufactured a false base of precisely the class it was accusing red of. What survives of blue's point is the framing defect only: red compared a segment cost line that now carries uranium cost against an SWU-only revenue line.
reopen_gates: PRINT (Q3, ~2026-11-04 or 2026-11-11, yfinance-derived UNCONFIRMED - prior-year Q3 8-K filed 2025-11-05): reopen only if the print BREAKS the $459M FY26 consensus in either direction. Above it with SWU realised price growth exceeding unit-cost growth -> reopen a long court. Below it -> the street was right and so were we; close the name.

DATA (the mechanism, from the MD&A's own price/volume/cost sentence): SWU average realised price growth vs SWU average unit cost growth. Q2 was +3% price against +13% unit cost; six months +16% against +23%. A quarter where price growth exceeds unit-cost growth is the margin squeeze ending and is the single cheapest read in the file - it is a sentence in the MD&A, not a model.

EVENT (supply): any replacement supply agreement priced at or below the 2018-adjusted TENEX contract level, or any change to Russian Decree No. 1516 (currently extended through 2027-12-31). The volume decline is contractual, not commercial, so the supply channel is where the earnings power is decided.

DATA (disclosure): a 10-K or 10-Q that reconciles company-defined backlog to ASC 606 RPO line by line - the reconciliation currently requires cross-reading the PR and the 10-Q, which is precisely how a red bench got to a masking verdict. Also: Q2 product-level gross-profit split (SWU margin ex-uranium), which the issuer withheld and which bounds only loosely today (SWU margin is somewhere between ~35.6% and 51.6% on the feasible range of uranium margin).

EVENT (funding reality): a DOE obligation appearing in USAspending under the Centrus/ACO/USEC family, or disclosed milestone-payment timing on the $900M firm-fixed-price task order. Red's null is non-probative today; a positive would convert 'funded' from a press-release word into an obligation record.

PRICE, REVIEW-ONLY AND CONDITIONED (replaces the bare alert_below 100): a $100 print is informative only if it is idiosyncratic - i.e. LEU is through $100 while URA/NLR and the enrichment complex are flat or up over the same window. A complex-wide drawdown that drags LEU to $100 is beta, not cheapness, and the beta-bleed doctrine says do not treat it as a dislocation.
process_findings: DIVERGENCE-NOT-COVERAGE VIOLATION CORRECTED (the batch's clearest instance): red's finding 6 killed court-worthiness on '17 analysts, 23% short interest'. Re-based - coverage is a measuring instrument, and 23% short against $1.87B of cash is a squeeze mechanic that conditions SIZE and TIMING. The valid kill, supplied by blue, is that the street's FY26 revenue number (~$459M) already sits at the bottom of the company's own $450-500M guide and FY26 EPS consensus was cut $2.90 -> $2.59. We agree with the street; that is the finding.

BLUE-CORRECTIONS-AUDITED - ONE PASS, ONE FAIL. PASS: the backlog/RPO overturn, verified verbatim in both venues by adjudicator re-fetch (desk/sec_fetch.py direct for the 10-Q text, direct fetch of the Q2 PR) and now reconciled exactly ($4.5B - $0.8B TS - $3.0B contingent = ~$0.7B LEU RPO). FAIL: blue's 'corrected' LEU segment base ($131.8M/$79.3M/$52.5M) is the intersegment-INCLUSIVE segment-note total compared against intersegment-free 2026 figures; the MD&A like-for-like is $125.7M/$75.0M/$50.7M, so red's $75.0M and +36% were verbatim correct and blue committed the base error it accused red of. Second consecutive batch in which the auditing bench needed auditing.

CONSENSUS PROVENANCE - THE KILL'S ONE SOFT SPOT: the $459.3M FY26 revenue consensus and the $2.90 -> $2.59 EPS revision are sourced to aggregators (simplywall.st, stockanalysis, a Yahoo estimate-revision piece), not to a primary consensus feed, and my WebSearch budget was exhausted before I could triangulate them. The verdict rests on this number, so it must be re-verified against a second independent aggregator before the row is graded for calibration. The company's own guide ($450-500M, verified at the PR by direct fetch) independently supports the direction: consensus sits at the bottom of the issuer's range.

MOAT-REFUTATION CHECK (2026-08-18): Western enrichment capacity expansion is NOT the bear case here. Realised SWU prices rose 3% in the quarter and 16% over six months while volumes fell on a Russian export-licence blockage - a supply-constrained market absorbing capacity at rising prices. The real bear leg is unit cost (+13% Q2, +23% six months) outrunning realised price.

HELD STATUS: NOT HELD. Ledger row exists (REVIEW_FLAG / WATCH, sleeve commodity_court, alert_below 100, '10x recurring gross profit'). THIS DRAFT RE-SPECIFIES THAT ALERT AS REVIEW-ONLY WITH A RELATIVE CONDITION (LEU through $100 while URA/NLR are flat-or-up), per the beta-carrier rule: roughly two-thirds of the drawdown is complex beta and an absolute price gate on that tape fires when the sector is worse, not when this business is cheaper.

CAP STRUCTURE, SUSTAINED IN FULL AND UNCONTESTED: 19,952,858 shares outstanding; convert principals $402.5M and $805.0M; 7.63M if-converted shares (+38.3%); NO capped call or note hedge disclosed anywhere in the 10-Q; if-converted EV ~$3.43B ~ 17.2x annualised gross profit. Any future per-share work on this name starts here (TENX discipline).
PRINT CLOCK: next print ~11-12 weeks out (2026-11-04/11, UNCONFIRMED) from 2026-08-17/18 - far outside the 5-day window, so no pre-print reconstruction was owed. Pre-print position FLAT.
TAX: no dividend; all return would be capital gain. The convert dilution is the relevant per-share drag, not any distribution.

DETECTOR DEFECTS LOGGED: sentinel2_buildout returned a 2021-01-19 baseline scene against a requested 2025 window with a generator-flagged lat/lon ~6km off - parcel identity unconfirmed, citable in neither direction. customs_id returned an empty consignee list, which cannot distinguish supply blockage from connector failure; red over-read it as corroboration. hiring_velocity fired AGAINST the bear case (Piketon ramp accelerating) and both benches conceded it honestly.

kg_candidates.name: asc606_rpo_gap_is_definitional_not_masking
kg_candidates.source: blue bench (LEU); adjudicator verified both venues and supplied the exact reconciliation
kg_candidates.disposition: ACCEPT AS PRIMARY, and it SUPERSEDES red's rpo_vs_marketed_backlog_divergence, which must be harvested only as a subordinate trigger behind this guard. Red's raw version would fire on essentially every ASC 606 filer with IDIQ or contingent volumes.
kg_candidates.one_line: Block a marketed-backlog-versus-RPO masking call whenever the filing itself states the exclusion rule (unexercised options, IDIQ, contingent commitments) and the marketed figure discloses its contingent component - the gap is definitional, and the test is whether backlog minus disclosed contingent minus IDIQ/options reproduces the RPO.
kg_candidates.fires_on: a bench asserts marketed_backlog/RPO divergence as concealment, AND the same filing contains an explicit RPO-exclusion sentence, AND the marketed figure discloses its contingent or unfunded component
kg_candidates.evidence_here: LEU Q2-2026, verified by adjudicator re-fetch: 10-Q states it 'does not include unexercised options or potential services under indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity agreements' and reports total RPO ~$0.8B (LEU segment ~$0.7B) to 2030; the PR states total backlog $4.5B to 2040, of which ~$3.0B is contingent LEU/HALEU commitments ($2.4B under definitive agreements) and ~$0.8B is Technical Solutions backlog including unfunded amounts and unexercised options. $4.5B - $0.8B - $3.0B = ~$0.7B = the LEU-segment RPO exactly.

kg_candidates.name: segment_note_intersegment_base_mismatch
kg_candidates.source: adjudicator (LEU) - found by re-fetching the primary to audit a BLUE correction
kg_candidates.disposition: ACCEPT - this is the batch's live BLUE-CORRECTIONS-AUDITED catch and it belongs in the KG because the failure is silent: both tables are in the same filing, both are labelled 'LEU segment', and only one is intersegment-eliminated.
kg_candidates.one_line: A segment-note total (intersegment-inclusive) compared against an MD&A segment table (intersegment-eliminated) manufactures a false growth base - always check whether the prior-period figure carries an 'intersegment, eliminated on consolidation' row before computing any segment growth rate.
kg_candidates.fires_on: any segment growth/margin computation where the two periods are drawn from different tables in the same filing, or where the prior period contains an intersegment line the current period does not
kg_candidates.evidence_here: LEU 10-Q: segment note shows LEU total revenue 2025 $131.8M (including $6.1M intersegment), cost of sales $79.3M (including $4.3M), gross profit $52.5M (including $1.8M); the MD&A table shows $125.7M / $75.0M / $50.7M. The blue bench used the segment-note 2025 base against the intersegment-free 2026 figures to 'correct' red, producing +16.4% revenue and +28.4% cost growth where the like-for-like is +22% and +36%. Red's original $75.0M base was verbatim correct.

kg_candidates.name: realized_price_vs_unit_cost_split
kg_candidates.source: adjudicator (LEU) - the mechanism sentence neither bench cited
kg_candidates.disposition: ACCEPT - for supply-constrained processors the MD&A price/volume/unit-cost sentence is the whole margin story, and both benches argued about aggregate cost lines while the filing stated the decomposition in words.
kg_candidates.one_line: For converters/processors/enrichers, read the MD&A's explicit price-volume-unit-cost sentence rather than the segment cost aggregate: realised price growth minus unit-cost growth is the margin signal, and an aggregate cost line polluted by a new product (here uranium) cannot produce it.
kg_candidates.fires_on: an issuer whose MD&A attributes cost-of-sales movement to 'average unit cost of X sold' and revenue movement to 'average price of X sold' - extract both percentages and difference them
kg_candidates.evidence_here: LEU Q2-2026: SWU volume -23%, average SWU price +3%, average SWU unit cost +13%; six months, volume -31%, price +16%, unit cost +23%. Segment gross margin 40.3% -> 33.6%. The cause is disclosed: TENEX 2018 pricing is blocked by Russian Decree No. 1516 through 2027-12-31 and replacement Orano SWU runs on a market formula to 2030.

packs_to_arm.date_confidence: yfinance-derived, UNCONFIRMED - no Centrus PR names a date; the prior-year Q3 8-K was filed 2025-11-05, so 11-04 or 11-11 are both plausible. Re-key on the company PR. Tier B because the kill is agreement-with-the-street: the pack exists to detect the street being WRONG, not to re-litigate what we already concede.
packs_to_arm.adjudication: Read in order: (1) FY26 revenue tracking against the $450-500M guide and the ~$459M consensus - a break either way is the reopen trigger and nothing else is; (2) the MD&A price/volume/unit-cost sentence for SWU - price growth versus unit-cost growth is the margin mechanism; (3) Technical Solutions gross margin, six-month basis not quarterly, against the fixed-price $900M task order and the Piketon hiring ramp (43 open reqs, 1->4->14->23 postings/month, guide of >=175 net new); (4) any product-level gross-profit split that separates SWU from uranium; (5) convert dilution and any capped-call disclosure - 7.63M shares of if-converted dilution with no hedge is the standing cap-structure fact; (6) any TENEX/Decree 1516 or replacement-supply development.

branches.REVENUE ABOVE THE GUIDE MIDPOINT WITH SW: the street's number breaks upward and the margin squeeze ends in the same print - reopen a long court on fresh benches; this is the only branch that changes the disposition.
branches.REVENUE NEAR $459M, MARGIN SQUEEZE PERSI: we and the street were both right; keep the name dead and stop spending court time on it.
branches.REVENUE BELOW GUIDE WITH TS STILL AT A G: deterioration beyond consensus; re-examine the short gate separately and on its own doctrine (borrow, squeeze risk at 23% short interest, cash of $1.87B) - do not assume a failed long is a short.
branches.REPLACEMENT SUPPLY SIGNED AT OR BELOW 20: the cost leg resolves independently of the demand leg; re-court on unit economics regardless of the revenue branch.
branches.10-K RECONCILES CONTINGENT BACKLOG TO RP: the disclosure defect that produced a false masking verdict is closed; update the KG guard and re-read the demand leg on the reconciled basis.
